section.name: The "caid" URI Scheme
section.t: A CAID is a syntactically valid URI : the scheme "caid" followed by ":" and a rootless path made of unreserved characters and ":". IANA is requested to register the scheme in the "Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) Schemes" registry with the following template :

dl.dd: caid
Provisional
dl.dt: Applications/protocols that use this scheme name:
dl.dd: Authorization receipts, permits, execution attestations, audit records, and other artifacts that identify an action by its Canonical Action Identifier.
Iman Schrock <team@emiliaprotocol.ai>
Iman Schrock <team@emiliaprotocol.ai>
This document.

section.t: Syntax: the caid rule of . Semantics: a caid URI identifies typed action content by digest. It is not a locator, and dereferencing it is undefined. Encoding: the identifier is ASCII and contains no percent-encoded octets; a percent-encoded form is not a CAID, and a carrying protocol removes any transport encoding before parsing. Interoperability: CAIDs are compared as exact strings (). treats scheme names as case-insensitive and makes lowercase the normal form; every CAID is already in that form, and a CAID parser refuses any other case, so an application that normalizes a URI before comparison obtains the same string. Security: and .

section.name: Media Types
section.t: This document registers no media type . A media type earns registration when a recipient must recognize a message by it, and no step of this document sends one of its objects that way:

ul.li: A type definition is configuration. A relying party pins it by definition_sha256 or by a registry digest (), and a definition obtained over the network is checked against that pin before use, never trusted for its label.
A mapping profile is pinned by its digest and comes from relying-party configuration; a label inside a presented artifact is never accepted as the profile or its source format ().
An enum snapshot is local by rule: computation and verification never fetch one ().
An action object travels inside the artifact that carries it, under that artifact's own format.

section.t: A specification that defines a transfer of any of these objects can register a media type for it.

section.name: Implementation Status
section.t: This section records the known implementations of this specification at the time of posting, as described in . Listing an implementation here does not imply endorsement by the IETF. The RFC Editor is asked to remove this section before publication.

EMILIA Protocol, Inc., the author's organization, maintains three implementations, in JavaScript, Python, and Go. Each implements decoding, parsing, computation, verification, the definition digest, and mapping for the jcs-sha256 suite, and refuses cbor-sha256 as unknown_suite. The JavaScript implementation uses only the platform's cryptographic library, and the Python and Go implementations use only their standard libraries. All three run one shared conformance corpus of core, mapping, and cross-format interoperability vectors, and a copy of the JavaScript implementation ships in the author's verification package. They are licensed under Apache-2.0 and published at <https://github.com/emiliaprotocol/emilia-protocol/tree/main/caid>. Contact: team@emiliaprotocol.ai.

All three implementations come from the author's organization, and none of them is independent. No independent implementation is known to the author. A party that runs these implementations or their conformance corpus reproduces the author's results; such external re-runs are reproductions, not independent implementations.

section.name: Changes since -03
section.t: This revision makes the processing model complete and checkable, and it is a substantive revision. Canonicalization, the suites, the digest, and the identifier format do not change. The lists below give every normative change. Each item in the first four lists is pinned by conformance vectors.

section.name: Newly Refused Inputs
section.t: This revision refuses each of the following inputs, which -03 accepted or did not address. The first four items refuse action objects whose CAIDs were valid under -03.

ul.li: Action objects nested deeper than 64 levels: malformed_json as JSON text, unsupported_value as host values (Sections and ).
Action objects whose canonical encoding exceeds 16,777,216 octets: unsupported_value ().
Strings and member names that contain a Unicode noncharacter, which I-JSON excludes: malformed_json as JSON text, unsupported_value as host values (Sections and ).
JSON text longer than 33,554,432 octets, even when the object it encodes is within the canonical limit: malformed_json ().

JSON text that begins with a byte order mark, is not valid UTF-8, is not exactly one JSON text, or contains NaN, Infinity, or an unescaped control character: malformed_json. lets a parser ignore a byte order mark; this profile refuses it.

JSON text with duplicate member names, including names that differ only in escaping: malformed_json. -03 required a raw parser to reject duplicates in its Security Considerations; the rule is now part of the decoder and has a reason.
Host values outside the data model, which an implementation now refuses instead of serializing as another value ().

Action objects under a nonconforming definition, or under two configured definitions of one type with different validation projections: invalid_definition (Sections and ). -03 did not say what a nonconforming definition does, so an implementation could issue a CAID that bound none of the intended fields.
Definitions with a field name that is empty, contains ":", is action_type, or repeats, and field entries of a registered field type that carry members the type does not define: invalid_definition ().
Timestamps with a lowercase "t" or "z", or with a second of 60, which permits and the -03 description "an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC" therefore admitted: mistyped_field ().
Identifiers that begin with "CAID:" or "Caid:", which the -03 ABNF admitted because an string literal is case-insensitive: malformed_caid ().
Amount strings whose integer part has a leading zero, such as "01.5", which the -03 prose admitted: invalid_amount ().

Identifiers whose suite begins with a digit, which the -03 suite ABNF already excluded, and identifiers whose digest's final character sets an unused bit, which -03 did not address: malformed_caid (). The reference implementations accepted both before this revision.

Mapping profiles with two rules for one source path, which -03 already forbade, a member whose value is null, a target_field that is not a string, a string outside its limit when measured in UTF-8 octets, or a target_action_type longer than 512 octets: invalid_mapping_profile ().

JSON text input (). Action objects and mapping sources received as text are decoded under an I-JSON profile, and every decoding failure is the single reason malformed_json. Definitions, registries, snapshots, and profiles get the same rules without the size limit.
The data model (), the number rule (), and one table of limits (). A literal that overflows binary64 is unsupported_number; one that underflows is the integer 0.
Host values (): refused, never rewritten, never an exception, and with the same result as the corresponding JSON text.

Reason order (). Computation phases 0 through 2 are gates that yield exactly one reason. The other phases all run, and their reasons are sorted by phase and field position and deduplicated, so unsupported_number always precedes unsupported_value.
Definition conformance and resolution (Sections and ). A field name is a non-empty string without ":", unique, and not action_type. The order of configured definitions no longer affects the result.
definition_sha256 (), which computation and verification report.
An expected definition_sha256 for verification, and the reason definition_mismatch ().
Verification details, one closed-shape entry per underlying reason ().
Status never affects computation or verification, so deprecated types resolve, compute, and verify ().
The code field type, named code formats, and the reason invalid_code ().
Field types match whole values, empty strings are present, and the integer type is value-based ().

The monotone enum advance () replaces the narrow correction rule of -03. The -03 sentences that treated any added value as a new type version are replaced; a relying party that needs exact reproducibility pins definition_sha256.
An option of the wrong type counts as absent ().
The accept-unregistered verifier option of -03 is removed. An object whose type has no definition fails verification as invalid_object with the detail unknown_action_type ().

The mapping profile member omitted_source_fields, the loss policy declared-source-semantic-loss, and the transform sha256-hex-to-digest (). The reference implementations and the shared interoperability corpus already used them; a mapper written from -03 refused such profiles.
Mapping limits, counted in UTF-8 octets: 1 to 128 rules, source paths of at most 2048 octets, profile strings of 1 to 512 octets, and omission reasons of 1 to 2048 octets ().
Mapping stages A through D, and the left: and right: composition of comparison reasons, are normative (Sections and ).
The mapper uses jcs-sha256 only when no suite is given ().

A grammatical suite outside the suite registry parses to unknown_suite instead of malformed_caid (). This changes verification step 1 of -03, "Strict-parse the CAID string ..., else malformed_caid": verification phase 1 now yields malformed_caid or unknown_suite (). The input is refused either way.
An unpaired surrogate escape in JSON text is malformed_json; in a host value it remains unsupported_value (Sections and ).
A string that fails amount-string is invalid_amount and a value that is not a string is mistyped_field; -03 allowed either reason for the former ().
A registered suite that an implementation does not implement parses, and computation and verification report it as unknown_suite; -03 left the verification reason unstated ().

The reference registry advances to registry version 5, with 62 type versions: 53 active, every one of which can compute, and 9 deprecated. dns.record.delete.1 and vendor.onboard.1 receive their first enum pins. key.create.2, key.rotate.2, firewall.rule.open.2, pii.export.2, and phi.disclose.2 resolve their open enums with existing field types. payment.refund.2, ach.debit.originate.2, rx.dispense.2, and prior.auth.approve.2 use code fields. contract.execute.2 requires both contract_value and currency; contract.execute.1 stays active for contracts that state no monetary value. The nine superseded version 1 types are deprecated and still resolve. Registry version 4 is kept byte for byte, and every type's definition_sha256 is published.

section.name: Other Changes
section.t: The following changes add or correct text without changing what an implementation accepts, refuses, or reports.

ul.li: A processing overview () and three appendices: the collected ABNF, now the only statement of every grammar, with case-sensitive strings ; the reason tables; and worked examples that recompute.
The identifier example of , which had no action object, is replaced by the example of . Long lines in examples are folded as specified in .

Security Considerations now cover truncation, replay, multiple identifiers, signature coverage, limits, code-format matching, confusables, and digest fields under suite migration. The parser requirements moved from Security Considerations to .
Privacy Considerations replace the statement that identifiers may be treated as public values with a confidentiality statement and the preimage-guessing risk.

IANA Considerations request six registries and a provisional URI scheme and explain why no media type is registered. The statement that the author's organization maintains the registries until adoption is removed.
An Implementation Status section .
Normative references to RFC 8259, RFC 3629, RFC 7405, RFC 7493, and RFC 3986, and informative references to RFC 7595, RFC 7942, RFC 8126, RFC 8792, and RFC 6838.
Wording that referred to earlier revisions as "this revision" is made revision-neutral.

section.name: Changes since -02
section.t: This revision makes enum validation replayable. External enum references now require a snapshot or edition label, a SHA-256 pin over the complete JCS values array, exact local resolution, and a verified membership check. Bare, unresolved, digest-mismatched, and out-of-set values fail closed.

The enum definition forms are now exact: a null member is present and malformed, compact inline members are trimmed of U+0020 SPACE only, a values array beside a compact inline reference must equal it, and an embedded values array beside an external reference is the pinned array. Values outside a compact inline list now fail closed.

Required-field presence means a member of the action object itself. Strings and member names containing an unpaired surrogate are refused as unsupported_value, making explicit the refusal that RFC 8785 already requires. Registries could correct an existing value-set pin in a new registry version under narrow conditions; -04 replaces that rule with the monotone advance of .

The reference registry advances from version 3 to version 4. It pins the SIX ISO 4217 List One snapshot published 2026-09-17 for every currency field, by values digest and by a digest over the whole snapshot file, and pins the Dispense As Written codes of rx.dispense.1 inline. Existing Action Objects containing a code in that snapshot produce the same CAID bytes; a code that version 3 accepted but the snapshot omits is refused. Eleven active types in the reference registry require an external value set that has no pinned snapshot yet and cannot produce a CAID under version 4 until one is published. Deployments must update their registry and enum-snapshot pins before reporting validation under registry v4. Historical v3 decisions remain decisions under the historical registry and are not retroactively relabeled v4.
This revision does not change the Action Object, identifier syntax, digest suites, or mapping algorithm, and changes canonicalization only by making the unpaired-surrogate refusal explicit.

section.name: Collected ABNF
section.t: This appendix collects every grammar of this document in the ABNF of , with the case-sensitive string syntax of . ALPHA, DIGIT, and HEXDIG are the core rules of . Each rule matches a string as a whole. Part A.1 is the identifier and part A.2 the digest syntax of each suite. Part A.3 holds the lexical field types, and part A.4 the registered code formats (), each named by its rule name. Part A.5 constrains definitions, part A.6 the mapping profile, and part A.7 accepts every reason of , including nested forms such as mapped_action:missing_material_field:amount. A timestamp's day is further limited by the length of its month ().

; A.2 Digest syntax per suite ; ; A suite whose digest is n octets encodes it in c = ceil(8n/6) ; base64url characters. The final character carries u = 6c - 8n ; unused low bits, which are zero: of the 64 base64url characters, ; only those whose 6-bit value is a multiple of 2^u may end the ; digest. For n = 32 (jcs-sha256 and cbor-sha256), c = 43 and ; u = 2.
